INSTRUCTIONS: TARGET DEFINITION TEMPLATE — Copy and edit for your scenario.
BEHAVIORS (pick one per target):
constant_velocity : Straight line at fixed heading.
gentle_turn       : Gradual heading change.
s_maneuver        : Evasive S-shaped path. Set turn_rate_dps (2-5 typical).
crossing          : Straight line from start_pos to end_pos.
orbit             : Circular holding pattern. Set orbit_radius_m (3000-5000).
approach          : Descending glide path from start_pos to end_pos.
departure         : Climbing away from start_pos to end_pos.
waypoints         : ★ CUSTOM — define your own [x,y,z] waypoints + times.
This gives you TOTAL control over the flight path.
COORDINATES: NED (North-East-Down). Z is NEGATIVE for altitude above ground.
[0, -20000, -5000] = at origin north, 20km south, 5km altitude.
TARGET SIZE (optional — affects detection probability at range):
rcs_dbsm: Radar Cross Section in dBsm. Examples:
-20 dBsm : small drone / bird
-10 dBsm : stealth UAV
0 dBsm : cruise missile / small fighter (clean)
5 dBsm : fighter jet (typical)
10 dBsm : small general aviation
20 dBsm : commercial airliner (737/A320)
30 dBsm : large transport (747/C-17)
40 dBsm : large ship / ground structure
If omitted, MATLAB uses its default RCS model.
DIMENSIONS (optional — for cuboid visualization):
dimensions: { length_m, width_m, height_m }
If omitted, target is rendered as a point.
LABEL (optional — shown in plots and metrics):
label: 'Boeing 737' or 'UAV Threat' etc.
CLASS_ID (optional — integer for target classification):
0 = unknown (default), 1 = aircraft, 2 = missile, etc.
You define the scheme. SSR/IFF sensors use this for identification.
